title: Shut a full kebab box: hold the springy lettuce leaf tucked in while the other hand shuts the lid and clicks its tabs
instruction: Close the kebab box for takeaway. Tuck any salad hanging over the rim back inside, close the lid, and push its tabs into their slots so they lock.
context: Fast food and counter workers (BLS: about 3.7 million in the US, 3.1 million in restaurants) shut a takeaway box on every hot meal that goes out in one. O*NET lists 'Wrap menu items such as sandwiches, hot entrees, and desserts for serving or for takeout' as a core task. A kebab box is filled to its rim, and a springy lettuce leaf over the edge flips back out when let go, so the worker holds it in with one hand while the other brings the lid down, then presses the lid's tabs into their slots. Food caught in the seam holds the lid about 2 mm proud, so the 2.5 mm barbs cannot reach under the flange and the box springs open in the bag.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline) in cm, heights above the counter. A moulded bagasse 9 x 6 in clamshell with tab lock (BioJX listing: 230 x 158 mm, 46 mm base, 80 mm shut, 30 g) stands on the counter centred at (32, 0), its 23 cm side along x. Its front, with the two tabs, faces the right arm (y = -7.9); the hinge runs along the left edge (y = +7.9). The lid rests open at about 73 degrees (its hinge spring's rest angle is 85, its weight sags it); shut, the spring pushes its front edge up with about 0.1 N, so an unlatched lid springs back up. Each of the two tabs, 5 cm either side of the middle as in the maker's photos, is a 20 mm wide strip hanging from the lid's front wall with a 2.5 mm barb on its inner face; it passes down through a 22 mm notch in the base's 12 mm front flange and the barb catches under the flange. In the base, about 350 g of doner kebab heaped to about 13 mm above the rim: nine portions of shaved meat strips, three pieces of shredded lettuce, three tomato slices, two onion rings, two pickled chilli peppers, and one lettuce leaf. The leaf's base lies on the heap under a meat portion, at the middle of the front, between the two tabs; another portion fills the box behind it to the far wall. Its tip, 35 x 39 mm, is hinged to the base 10 mm inside the front rim and sticks about 23 mm out past the front wall's outer face (about 10 mm past the flange's edge), rising about 10 degrees; folded back in and let go, it springs back out. Bagasse on bagasse friction 0.5, food 0.7. Real trial: the box from the listing, cooked doner meat and fresh salad from one shop, weighed and laid out to a photo of this layout; a fresh box every trial. Barbs count as caught when the box lifted by its shut lid stays shut. Tab bend, lid spring and leaf spring should be measured on real parts; here they are estimates from product photos.
scoring: 1.0 at the end: both tabs' barbs caught under the flange (real trial: at each notch, the barb is seen hooked under the flange in a photo from the front or below), no food outside the shut lid's outline (real trial: photo from above), the box flat (real trial: judged from the trial video), both grippers 3 cm clear and still for 2 s (real trial: a 3 cm wooden block as a gauge, and a phone timer). Otherwise the highest substep reached: 0.7 the lid down (real trial: highest reached during the run; a phone on a tripod at flange height films the front, a 10 mm block on the flange beside a tab gives scale, and the lid counts as down in any frame where its front edge is at or below the block top) with every food piece inside, a clean seam (real trial: a photo along the front shows nothing between lid and flange); 0.3 the lid down with food in the seam or outside the box. 0: the box tipped past 30 degrees (real trial: judged from the trial video) or left the counter.
reset_notes: A fresh box with its lid sprung open and the same food in the same places, the leaf's tip over the front rim; arms at their start pose. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Rigid bodies on GPU. The lid is a rigid shell on a sprung hinge; each tab a sprung strip whose barb hooks under a notched flange, so latching is contact. The leaf is drawn as an irregular sheet; it is two rigid plates on a sprung hinge standing in for its stiffness, so a folded tip springs back. Other food is rigid. Spring values are estimates. The demo reads the box's pose and its lid's and leaf's joint angles, which a policy does not get.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0, valid, one session, 2,000 steps; demo: 1.0
